records.learner: Good question. The postMessage from Centrobill only refreshes the UI, it never unlocks anything by itself, because anyone can fake a message from the console. The real access is granted when Centrobill's server sends the postback to our route, we verify it there, and we write the access row in Supabase. And that row is protected by Row Level Security, so even if someone calls the API directly, the database only returns what that user is allowed to see. So the browser message just tells the screen to check again, and the server decides who pays.
records.planted_point: Says the RLS on the access row is what verifies the payment / makes the unlock safe, when the correct mechanism is: the server postback is verified and writes the access row; RLS only limits what each user can read or write, it doesn't validate the payment itself.

records.learner: Sure. It's five weekly milestones plus a QA week, and every Wednesday the code is on your GitHub and on Vercel staging. Week one is the foundation: the full schema in Supabase, row-level security on every table, the 45/55 split, and the private buckets. Week two is protection: the 120-second signed links, the protected reader, and the Sunday leaderboard reset. Week three is the creator side: the upload portal, the AI scan that flags safe or adult content, auto-cropping into vertical panels, and the price floors. Week four is payments: the Centrobill iframe and postback, the paywall at chapter four, and the 18-plus gate. Week five is payouts and revenue: the Paxum payout ledger, the ad slots for non-paying readers, and the print-on-demand webhooks. Week six is only testing and polish, with sign-off on December 24th.

records.learner: Good question. Since the ledger never deletes or edits a row, a refund is just a new entry that moves the money back, so the balance is always the sum of all entries. For a chargeback, I would write a negative transaction in the same way, and the creator's 55% balance goes down automatically. Actually I have not build this exact case before, but the pattern is the same one I used in Valley of Guardians, where every movement was a new row.
records.planted_point: 'Since the ledger never deletes' → 'Because the ledger never deletes' (since is not used for cause); 'I have not build' → 'I have not built' (wrong participle after have).

records.learner: The 55% goes back too, so the creator's balance decreases by the same amount as the refunded sale. We write a negative entry for the creator's share and another for the platform's share, both in the same transaction, so the split stays exact. That way the sum of the ledger always matches what the creator can withdraw.
